learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Dynamics formulations used in Classical Mechanics, necessary for the design of machine mechanisms.
Use of multi-body models for kinematic analysis of a machine.

Have the ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve problems of kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies and simple mechanisms and machines using established methods.
Have the ability to design and carry out experiments in the theory of machines and mechanisms, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Have the ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods to solve problems of kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies, simple mechanisms and machines.
Have an understanding of methods and techniques applicable in the theory of machines and mechanisms and their limitations.

syllabus_topics: Principles of kinematics and dynamics of planar and spatial mechanisms
Dynamic analysis of machines and mechanisms using classical mechanics
Applications of analytical mechanics to the study of mechanisms
teaching_methods: Theoretical-practical content sessions in Teaching Groups
Work Group sessions for manual problem statement and resolution, followed by computer implementation for advanced analysis and simulations using Matlab/Simulink and Simscape Multibody toolbox
Monitoring mechanisms for autonomous student work supported by Blackboard tools
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.6 * Activity 1 + 0.2 * Activity 2 + 0.2 * Activity 3. To pass the course, a grade greater than 4 must be obtained in the ordinary or extraordinary final exam. If a final grade of 5 or higher is not achieved in the ordinary call, students may keep the grades of the activities they deem convenient for the extraordinary call of the same academic year. Late submission of the final assignment (Activity 3) will result in a deduction of 0.5 points out of 10 for each calendar day of delay.
